acceptance_criteria.text: A name of 1 to 50 characters and a message of 1 to 500 characters (after trimming, counted as visible characters) are accepted; empty, whitespace-only, 51-character names and 501-character messages are rejected, on a direct submission as well as in the form. A rejected submission keeps the typed text, shows errors beside the fields and stores nothing.

Approved messages are listed newest first, 20 per page, with working Older/Newer links, a page number in the URL, clamping of out-of-range or invalid page numbers, and an empty-state message when there are none.
Message and name text containing HTML or Markdown is displayed literally and escaped, never executed or interpreted; line breaks in messages are preserved.

A valid submission is stored as pending and not shown publicly; the visitor is redirected to a page saying "Thanks, your message will appear once it's approved.", the form is cleared, and reloading doesn't resubmit it. Pending messages appear in no public list or count.

The owner page, protected by a secret token, lists pending messages and lets the owner approve or delete each one. Approving makes the message appear publicly, ordered by when it was left; deleting removes it. Without a correct token nothing is shown or changed, and with no token configured the owner page is disabled.

Only name, message, time and approval status are stored for a message. Messages, pending or approved, older than 12 months are deleted automatically (at startup and daily), while younger ones are kept. Visitors have no way to edit or delete their message.

A submission with the hidden honeypot filled looks successful but isn't stored. The fourth submission by one visitor within 10 minutes is refused with a try-again-later message that keeps the typed text, and is accepted after the window passes. There is no CAPTCHA.

Messages are stored in SQLite and survive a restart, concurrent submissions are all stored, and a storage failure shows a plain unavailable message without technical details. The service runs locally by following guestbook/README.md; no hosting setup is required.

All guestbook code lives in guestbook/ and the change doesn't add to, edit or depend on anything outside that folder (apart from specs/), including the to-do app from #10. The public page needs no token or secret link to read.
The public page and the owner page can be used by keyboard alone and on a narrow phone screen without sideways scrolling, with labelled fields and announced errors and confirmation.
